rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel is Jacob, peace be upon him; the name is his title and means God's chosen in their language.
rows.anchor: هو يعقوب عليه السلام لقب له ومعناه في لسانهم صفوة الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss gives Israel the meaning servant of God.
rows.anchor: ومعناه في لسانهم صفوة الله وقيل عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel follows the morphological pattern of Abraham and Ishmael and is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name.
rows.anchor: وهو بزنة إبراهيم وإسماعيل غير منصرف مثلهما لوجود العلمية والعجمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two variant pronunciations of Israel are read.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( اسرائل ) و ( اسرائل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the blessing requires gratitude, recognition and magnification of it, and obedience to its giver.
rows.anchor: وذكرهم النعمة ان لا يخلو بشكرها ويعتدوا بها ويستعظموها ويطيعوا مانحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings include the ancestors' rescue from Pharaoh and drowning, forgiveness after the calf, and their repentance.
rows.anchor: من الإنجاء من فرعون وعذابه ومن الغرق ومن العفو عن إتخاذ العجل والتوبة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing also includes their reaching Muhammad's time, since the Torah and Gospel had announced him.
rows.anchor: وما أنعم به عليهم من إدراك زمن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم المبشر به في التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant may be grammatically ascribed to either covenanting party: fulfilling one's covenant means fulfilling what one pledged, while fulfilling another's means the promise made to that person.
rows.anchor: والعهد يضاف إلى المعاهد والمعاهد جميعا يقال أوفيت بعهدي أي عاهدت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites must fulfill their pledge to believe in God and obey Him.
rows.anchor: واوفوا بما عاهدتموني عليه من الإيمان بي والطاعة لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's fulfillment of His covenant means granting the excellent reward for their good deeds.
rows.anchor: بما عاهدتكم عليه من حسن الثواب على حسناتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God means not breaking His covenant; the fronted object gives stronger exclusivity than in the expression You alone we worship.
rows.anchor: فلا تنقضوا عهدي وهو من قولك زيدا رهبته وهو اوكد في افادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with a doubled f intensifies the promise: God will fulfill the covenant abundantly.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( واوف ) بالتشديد أي أبالغ في الوفاء بعهدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant may specifically mean their pledge to believe in the Prophet of Mercy and the miraculous Scripture, as the following command to believe indicates.
rows.anchor: ما عاهدوا عليه ووعدوه من الإيمان بنبي الرحمة والكتاب المعجز ويدل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First disbeliever may mean the first individual, faction or group to reject the revelation, or each Israelite as the first such disbeliever.
rows.anchor: أول من كفر به أو اول فريق أو فوج كافر به أو ولا يكن كل واحد منكم اول كافر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke implies they should have believed first: they knew Muhammad's description, had announced his time, and had expected his followers to precede all people, yet acted oppositely after his mission.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعريض بأنه كان يجب أن يكونوا أول من يؤمن به لمعرفتهم به وبصفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scriptural passages say the People of the Book divided only after clear proof came and that they rejected what they recognized.
rows.anchor: وما تفرق الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation warns them not to resemble the first disbelievers, meaning the Meccan polytheists who lacked scripture and knowledge of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد ولا تكونوا مثل أول كافر به يعني من أشرك به من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'disbelieve in it' may refer to what is with the Israelites, since rejecting what confirms it amounts to rejecting it.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير في ( به ) لما معكم لأنهم اذا كفروا بما يصدقه فقد كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buying is a metaphor for exchanging one thing for another, as in the verse about exchanging guidance for error.
rows.anchor: والاشتراء استعارة للاستبدال كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small price was leadership among their people, which they feared losing by following the Messenger; compared with God's signs and truth, every worldly return is little.
rows.anchor: والثمن القليل الرياسة التى كانت لهم في قومهم خافوا عليها الفوات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Common people paid their scribes in crops, fruit and gifts, and bribed them to distort Scripture and ease difficult laws; rulers also funded concealment or distortion.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانت عامتهم يعطون أحبارهم من زروعهم وثمارهم ويهدون اليهم الهدايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people had been farmers; returning to their old habits made them weary of their blessing and desirous of misery.
rows.anchor: كانوا فلاحة فنزعوا إلى عكرهم فاجموا ما كانوا فيه من النعمة وطلبت انفسهم الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single food means manna and quails, called one because they did not vary; even a varied daily menu could be called one food if unchanged.
rows.anchor: أرادوا ما رزقوا في التيه من المن والسلوى فإن قلت هما طعامان فما لهم قالوا على طعام واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the two foods were one kind because both belonged to luxurious eating, while the farming people wanted their familiar varied grains and vegetables.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يريدوا انهما ضرب واحد لأنهما معا من طعام اهل التلذذ والتترف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb 'bring forth' means to make appear and produce.
rows.anchor: يظهر لنا ويوجد والبقل ما أنبتته الأرض من الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested greens are choice vegetables eaten by people, such as mint, celery and leek.
rows.anchor: والمراد به اطايب البقول التى يأكلها الناس كالنعناع والكرفس والكراث وأشباهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading vocalizes the word for cucumbers with a damma.
rows.anchor: وقرىء وقثائها ) بالضم والفوم الحنطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fūm means wheat, supported by the idiom 'bring us wheat' meaning bake bread.
rows.anchor: والفوم الحنطة ومنه فوموا لنا أي اخبزوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes fūm to mean garlic; Ibn Masud's reading 'and its garlic' supports it and better pairs it with lentils and onions.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة إبن مسعود ( وثومها ) وهو للعدس والبصل اوفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā means lower in rank and smaller in value; nearness and distance can metaphorically indicate low and high worth.
rows.anchor: الذي هو أقرب منزلة وأدون مقدارا والدنو والقرب يعبر بهما عن قلة المقدار

rows.speaker: زهير الفرقبي
rows.claim: Zuhayr al-Farqabī reads adnaʾ with hamza, deriving it from meanness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زهير الفرقبي ( أدنأ ) بالهمزة من الدناءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with a damma means descend to the place from the wilderness; h-b-ṭ can mean entering a valley or leaving it.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( اهبطوا ) بالضم أي انحدروا اليه من التيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wilderness extended from Jerusalem to Qinnasrin, twelve farsakhs by eight.
rows.anchor: وبلاد التيه ما بين بيت المقدس إلى قنسرين وهي إثنا عشر فرسخا في ثمانية فراسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miṣran may be the proper name of Egypt; it is declined despite properness and femininity because its middle consonant is quiescent, like Noah and Lot.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد العلم وإنما صرفه مع اجتماع السببين فيه وهما التعريف والتأنيث لسكون وسطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means the country, it has only one of the two causes of indeclinability; if it means any city, it is indefinite, while Abdullah's codex and al-Aʿmash read the city name without tanwin.
rows.anchor: وإن أريد به البلد فما فيه الا سبب واحد وان يريد مصرا من الأمصار وفي مصحف عبد الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies Egypt with Miṣrāyim, an Arabized form.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مصرائيم فعرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humiliation surrounds them like a tent, or sticks to them like plaster; Jews are lowly and destitute either in reality or by feigning poverty to avoid a higher poll tax.
rows.anchor: جعلت الذلة محيطة بهم مشتملة عليهم فهم فيها كما يكون في القبة من ضربت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To incur God's wrath means to become deserving of it, like someone who merits being killed in retaliation for an equal victim.
rows.anchor: من قولك باء فلان بفلان اذا كان حقيقا بان يقتل به لمساواته له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to humiliation, indigence and incurring wrath, caused by disbelief and killing prophets; the Jews killed Isaiah, Zechariah, John and others.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والخلاقة بالغضب أي ذلك بسبب كفرهم وقتلهم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although prophet-killing is inherently unjust, 'without right' means even by their own standards the prophets had committed no offense deserving death; they only advised them.
rows.anchor: معناه انهم قتلوهم بغير الحق عندهم لأنهم لم يقتلوا ولا أفسدوا في الأرض

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali reads the verb with gemination, emphasizing repeated killing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه ( ويقتلون ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated demonstrative reiterates the previous reference.
rows.anchor: تكرار للاشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disobedience means committing many sins and transgressing God's limits in every matter, alongside disbelief and prophet-killing.
rows.anchor: بسبب إرتكابهم أنواع المعاصي وإعتدائهم حدود الله في كل شيء مع كفرهم بآيات الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view specifies their transgression as violating the Sabbath.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو إعتداؤهم في السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative may point back to disbelief and killing as the result of persistent disobedience and transgression, which hardened hearts until they dared deny signs and kill prophets.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يشار بذلك إلى الكفر وقتل الأنبياء على معنى أن ذلك بسبب عصيانهم واعتدائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to the disbelief and killing together with their other disobedience.
rows.anchor: أو ذلك الكفر والقتل مع ما عصوا

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The fools may be Jews who disliked facing the Kaaba and denied the possibility of abrogation.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود لكراهتهم التوجه إلى الكعبة وانهم لا يرون النسخ

rows.speaker: المنافقون
rows.claim: Another identification is the hypocrites, eager to find grounds for criticism and mockery.
rows.anchor: وقيل المنافقون لحرصهم على الطعن والاستهزاء

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: A third identification is the polytheists, who said Muhammad first rejected his fathers' qibla, then returned, and would return to their religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل المشركون قالوا رغب عن قبلة آبائه ثم رجع اليها والله ليرجعن إلى دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Announcing their objection in advance softens the shock, prepares believers for it and supplies a ready answer that more effectively silences the opponent.
rows.anchor: فائدته ان مفاجأة المكروه أشد والعلم به قبل وقوعه أبعد من الاضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks who turned them away; the former qibla was Jerusalem.
rows.anchor:
﴿ ما ولاهم ﴾
ما صرفهم
﴿ عن قبلتهم ﴾
وهي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The east and west mean the lands in those directions and the whole earth.
rows.anchor: أي بلاد المشرق والمغرب والأرض كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides whom He wills from among the earth's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: من اهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the wise and beneficial choice to direct the community first to Jerusalem and then to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وهو ما توجبه الحكمة والمصلحة من توجيههم تارة إلى بيت المقدس وأخرى إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compares the community's appointment to that remarkable arrangement.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك الجعل العجيب جعلناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasatan means the best; it is an adjectival use of the noun for a thing's middle and therefore has the same form for singular, plural and all genders.
rows.anchor: خيارا وهي صفة بالاسم الذي هو وسط الشيء ولذلك استوى فيه الواحد والجمع والمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic expression about giving the thabja refers to the middle animal, between fat and thin, describing it by its back's middle.
rows.anchor:
ونحوه قوله عليه السلام
63 ( وأنطوا الثبجة )
+ + يريد الوسيطة بين السمينة والعجفاء وصفا بالثج وهو وسط الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle is called the best because the edges are prone to defects while the protected center remains sound; al-Ta'i's verse illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: وقيل للخيار وسط لأن الأطراف يتسارع اليها الخلل والأعوار والأوساط محمية محوطة

rows.speaker: الطائي
rows.claim: Al-Ta'i uses wasat for a protected center that later becomes an edge amid surrounding events.
rows.anchor: ( كانت هي الوسط المحمي فاكتنفت … بها الحوادث حتى أصبحت طرفا )

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: A Meccan Bedouin asked for the middle of his coins, meaning the best or fairest ones, since the middle is equally distant from both extremes.
rows.anchor: وقد اكتريت بمكة جمل اعرابي للحج فقال أعطني من سطاتهنه

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: On Judgment Day nations deny that their prophets conveyed the message; Muhammad's community testifies from God's revealed Book, and Muhammad then attests to their uprightness.
rows.anchor:
﴿ لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ﴾ روي
64 ( أن الأمم يوم القيامة يجحدون تبليغ الأنبياء فيطالب الله الأنبياء بالبينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's testimony is linked to God's bringing a witness from every nation and Muhammad as witness over them.
rows.anchor:
+ + وذلك قوله تعالى
﴿ فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا ﴾ النساء 41

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition 'over' is used because a witness is like a supervisor and guardian over the person witnessed for.
rows.anchor: لما كان الشهيد كالرقيب والمهيمن على المشهود له جيء بكلمة الاستعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the community testifies in this life wherever trustworthy, upright witnesses are required, while the Messenger validates and knows their uprightness.
rows.anchor: وقيل لتكونوا شهداء على الناس في الدنيا فيما لا يصح إلا بشهادة العدول الأخيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause delays the object of testimony to emphasize witnessing over nations; the second advances it to single out the Messenger's testimony over this community.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرض في الأول اثبات شهادتهم على الأمم وفي الآخر اختصاصهم بكون الرسول شهيدا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is not an adjective of qibla but the second object of 'made': the intended direction is the Kaaba faced in Mecca, before Jerusalem was prescribed after migration to conciliate Jews and then the Kaaba restored as a test.
rows.anchor: ليست بصفة للقبلة انما هي ثاني مفعولي جعل يريد وما جعلنا القبلة الجهة التى كنت عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test distinguishes a steadfast, sincere Muslim from someone unstable who turns back.
rows.anchor: الثابت على الاسلام الصادق فيه ممن هو على حرف ينكص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Jerusalem's temporary qibla was set to test who follows the Messenger and who turns away, since the original command was to face the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بيانا للحكمة في جعل بيت المقدس قبلته يعني ان أصل أمرك ان تستقبل الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back on one's heels means apostasy.
rows.anchor: لقلقه فيرتد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet faced Jerusalem in Mecca while placing the Kaaba between himself and Jerusalem.
rows.anchor:
وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
65 ( كانت قبلته بمكة بيت المقدس الا أنه كان يجعل الكعبة بينه وبينه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's 'so that We know' means making the matter known in an actualized form to which recompense attaches, not acquiring previously absent knowledge.
rows.anchor: ان يعلمه موجودا حاصلا ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the purpose is for the Messenger and believers to know; knowledge is ascribed to God because they are His chosen and favored people.
rows.anchor: وقيل ليعلم رسول الله والمؤمنون وإنما أسند علمهم إلى ذاته لأنهم خواصه وأهل الزلفى عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is to distinguish the follower from the one turning back; knowledge stands for the distinction made through knowing.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه لنميز التابع من الناكص كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'though it was difficult,' inna is the lightened form of the emphatic particle and requires the distinguishing lām.
rows.anchor: هي إن المخففة التى تلزمها اللام الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to the implied change, apostasy, conversion or appointment indicated by the previous clause, or directly to the qibla.
rows.anchor:
﴿ كانت ﴾
لما دل عليه قوله
^ وما جعلنا القبلة التي كانت عليها ^
من الردة أو التحويلة أو الجعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabīra means burdensome and difficult.
rows.anchor:
﴿ لكبيرة ﴾
لثقيلة شاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided are the sincere, steadfast followers whom God graciously favored and who were worthy of that favor.
rows.anchor: الا على الثابتين الصادقين في اتباع الرسول الذين لطف الله بهم وكانوا أهلا للطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not waste the community's faith: they remained firm without wavering or doubt, and He has prepared a great reward for them.
rows.anchor: أي ثباتكم على الإيمان وأنكم لم تزلوا ولم ترتابوا بل شكر صنيعكم وأعد لكم الثواب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God could not leave the qibla unchanged because that would damage and waste the believers' faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد وما كان الله ليترك تحويلكم لعلمه ان تركه مفسدة وإضاعة لإيمانكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The prayers offered toward Jerusalem before the change are not lost.
rows.anchor: وقيل من كان صلى إلى بيت المقدس قبل التحويل فصلاته غير ضائعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: When the Messenger turned toward the Kaaba, people asked about their fellow believers who had died before the change; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor:
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
66 لما وجه رسول الله إلى الكعبة قالوا كيف بمن مات قبل التحويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is compassionate and merciful because He neither loses their reward nor withholds what benefits them.
rows.anchor: لا يضيع أجورهم ولا يترك ما يصلحهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When al-Hajjaj asked Hasan about Abu Turab, Hasan identified Ali as among those guided, citing his kinship, marriage to the Prophet's daughter, closeness and love.
rows.anchor:
ويحكى عن الحجاج أنه قال للحسن ما رأيك في أبي تراب فقرأ قوله
﴿ إلا على الذين هدى الله ﴾
ثم قال وعلي منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading of 'so that it be known' is reported, with knowledge meaning recognition.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( الا ليعلم ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word man may carry an interrogative sense that suspends the verb 'know,' as in asking whether Zayd or Amr is in the house.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان تكون ( من ) متضمنة لمعنى الاستفهام معلقا عنها العلم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq reads the qāf of ʿaqibayhi as quiescent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( على عقبيه ) بسكون القاف

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazidi reads kabīra in the nominative, taking kāna as extra; the underlying construction is 'it is certainly difficult,' supported by a poetic example.
rows.anchor: وقرأ اليزيدي ( لكبيرة ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading doubles the yāʾ in 'waste.'
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ليضيع ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Do not disbelieve' means do not deny God's blessings.
rows.anchor:
﴿ ولا تكفرون ﴾
ولا تجحدوا نعمائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The martyrs are not dead but alive, though people cannot perceive the manner of their life.
rows.anchor:
﴿ أموات بل أحياء ﴾
هم أموات بل هم أحياء
﴿ ولكن لا تشعرون ﴾
كيف حالهم في حياتهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says martyrs live with God: their provisions are shown to their souls and they receive comfort and joy, just as Pharaoh's people see the Fire and feel pain morning and evening.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ان الشهداء أحياء عند الله تعرض أرزاقهم على أرواحهم فيصل اليهم الروح والفرح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says martyrs receive Paradise's fruit and scent without being inside it.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد يرزقون ثمر الجنة ويجدون ريحها وليسوا فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God may gather the martyr's scattered parts into a whole and give them life and bliss even if they are tiny as a speck.
rows.anchor: وقالوا يجوز ان يجمع الله من اجزاء الشهيد جملة فيحييها ويوصل اليها النعيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is also said that the verse was revealed about the fourteen martyrs of Badr.
rows.anchor: وقيل نزلت في شهداء بدر وكانوا أربعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one and unique in divinity, with no partner; no other being can rightly be called a god.
rows.anchor: فرد في الإلهية لا شريك له فيها ولا يصح ان يسمى غيره إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'There is no deity but Him' restates oneness by denying all others and affirming God alone.
rows.anchor: تقرير للوحدانية بنفي غيره واثباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful and Compassionate is the source of every basic and derivative blessing; no other being has this quality, since all else is either blessing or recipient of blessing.
rows.anchor: المولى لجميع النعم أصولها وفروعها ولا شيء سواه بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that when the polytheists, who had 360 idols around the Kaaba, heard the verse they demanded a sign of Muhammad's truth, and verse 164 followed.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان للمشركين حول الكعبة ثلثمائة وستون صنما فلما سمعوا بهذه الآية تعجبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete Hajj and Umrah fully, performing their rites and conditions for God's sake without slackness or omission.
rows.anchor: ائتوا بهما تامين كاملين بمناسكهما وشرائطهما لوجه الله من غير توان ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem treats stopping at Khurqa with face uncovered as one of the acts needed to complete pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: ( تمام الحج ان تقف المطايا … على خرقاء واضعة اللثام )

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Another interpretation says completion means entering ihram for both rites from one's home.
rows.anchor: وقيل اتمامهما أن تحرم بهما من دويرة اهلك روى ذلك عن علي وابن عباس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A view says each rite should have its own journey, with a Kufa Hajj and Kufa Umrah preferred.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان تفرد لكل واحد منهما سفرا كما قال محمد حجة كوفية وعمرة كوفية أفضل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes lawful expenditure part of completing the rites.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان تكون النفقة حلالا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation requires dedicating both rites to worship without mixing them with trade or worldly aims.
rows.anchor: وقيل ان تخلصوهما للعبادة ولا تشوبوهما بشيء من التجارة والأغراض الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to complete both rites does not by itself establish whether Umrah is obligatory or voluntary, since either can be completed; a command to perform them and the default force of commands could argue for obligation absent contrary proof.
rows.anchor: ولا دليل في ذلك على كونهما واجبين أو تطوعين فقد يؤمر بإتمام الواجب والتطوع جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to complete Umrah does not prove its obligation; reports say it is not obligatory like Hajj though performing it is better, and that Hajj is jihad while Umrah is voluntary.
rows.anchor: 101 أنه قيل يا رسول الله العمرة واجبة مثل الحج قال ( لا ولكن أن تعتمر خير لك )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls Hajj jihad and Umrah voluntary.
rows.anchor:
وعنه
102 ( الحج جهاد والعمرة تطوع )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls Umrah the companion of Hajj; the author says this means they are paired in qiran and in common mention, not equal in obligation.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت فقد روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال إن العمرة لقرينة الحج

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A man said he found Hajj and Umrah prescribed for him and entered ihram for both; Umar replied that he had followed the Prophet's practice.
rows.anchor:
وعن عمر رضي الله عنه
103 ان رجلا قال له إني وجدت الحج والعمرة مكتوبين علي أهللت بهما جميعا فقال ( هديت لسنة نبيك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Umrah the companion of Hajj refers to pairing them in a combined pilgrimage, in speech, or as the lesser pilgrimage; none establishes equal obligation.
rows.anchor: كونها قرينة للحج ان القارن يقرن بينهما وانهما يقترنان في الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar's report means the man's undertaking became binding when he entered ihram, just as beginning a voluntary prayer with the opening takbir makes it binding.
rows.anchor: وإذا أهل بالعمرة وجبت عليه كما اذا كبر بالتطوع من الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence leaves Hajj obligatory and Umrah voluntary, as in an instruction combining Ramadan fasting with a voluntary six days of Shawwal.
rows.anchor: فبقي الحج وحده فيها فهما بمنزلة قولك صم شهر رمضان وستة من شوال

rows.speaker: علي وابن مسعود والشعبي رضي الله عنهم
rows.claim: They read 'and Umrah is for God' in the nominative, apparently separating Umrah from Hajj's obligatory ruling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وابن مسعود والشعبي رضي الله عنهم ( والعمرة لله ) بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is muḥṣar when fear, illness or incapacity prevents travel; the verb is used for prevention generally.
rows.anchor: يقال أحصر فلان إذا منعه امر من خوف أو مرض أو عجز

rows.speaker: ابن ميادة
rows.claim: Ibn Mayyada's line uses the verb for being prevented by preoccupation from reaching Layla.
rows.anchor: ( وما هجر ليلى ان تكون تباعدت … عليك ولا ان أحصرتك شغول )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣara usually means an enemy blocks or imprisons someone; ḥaṣīr can name a prison or king because he is shielded.
rows.anchor: وحصر اذا حبسه عدو عن المضي أو سجن ومنه قيل للمحبس الحصير

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عمرو الشيباني وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Farra, Abu Amr al-Shaybani and Abu Hanifa treat the verbs as overlapping: any prevention, whether enemy, illness or otherwise, establishes ihsar.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال الفراء وابو عمرو الشيباني وعليه قول أبي حنيفة رحمهم الله تعالى كل منع عنده من عدو كان أو مرض

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafi'i limit legally recognized ihsar to prevention by an enemy.
rows.anchor: وعند مالك والشافعي منع العدو وحده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that one whose bone is broken or who becomes lame may exit ihram and must perform Hajj the following year.
rows.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
104 ( من كسر أو عرج فقد حل وعليه الحج من قابل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā istaysara means whatever is readily available; istaysara is patterned like istasʿaba from ṣaʿuba.
rows.anchor: فما تيسر منه يقال يسر الأمر واستيسر كما يقال صعب واستصعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadī is the plural of hadiyya, as jadī is the plural form of the saddle's jadya; a doubled reading gives the plural hadāyā.
rows.anchor: والهدى جمع هدية كما يقال في جدية السرج جدي وقرىء ( من الهدي ) بالتشديد جمع هدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those prevented while in Hajj or Umrah ihram who wish to exit must sacrifice whatever is readily available of camel, cow or sheep.
rows.anchor: فعليكم اذا أردتم التحلل ما استيسر من الهدي من بعير أو بقرة أو شاة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: For an obstructed pilgrim, Abu Hanifa permits sacrifice in the sanctuary at any time and requires sending the animal with a date designated for the representative; his two disciples require the Hajj sacrifice days.
rows.anchor: ان كان حاجا فبالحرم متى شاء عند أبي حنيفة يبعث به ويجعل للمبعوث على يده يوم أمار وعندهما في أيام النحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An obstructed person performing Umrah sacrifices in the sanctuary at any time, by agreement among the cited jurists.
rows.anchor: وإن كان معتمرا فبالحرم في كل وقت عندهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'whatever is readily available' may be nominative as an implied subject, or accusative under an implied command to offer it.
rows.anchor: و ( ما استيسر ) رفع بالابتداء أي فعليه ما استيسر أو نصب على فاهدوا ما استيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on shaving addresses the obstructed pilgrims: they may not exit until sure their offering has reached the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للمحصرين أي لا تحلوا حتى تعلموا ان الهدي الذي بعثتموه إلى الحرم بلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥill means the place where an offering must be slaughtered; the parallel sense of a debt's due time or place supports Abu Hanifa's view.
rows.anchor: أي مكانه الذي يجب نحره فيه ومحل الدين وقت وجوب قضائه وهو ظاهر على مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet sacrificed where he was obstructed, Hudaibiyya's lower-Makkah edge lies within the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: كان محصره طرف الحديبية الذي إلى أسفل مكة وهو من الحرم

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Messenger sacrificed his offering in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor:
+ 125 + وعن الزهري
106 ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحر هديه في الحرم

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Waqidi places Hudaibiyya at the sanctuary's edge, nine miles from Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال الواقدي الحديبية هي طرف الحرم على تسعة أميال من مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick person is one whose illness makes shaving necessary.
rows.anchor: فمن كان به مرض يحوجه إلى الحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Head irritation means lice or a wound; shaving it incurs an expiation.
rows.anchor: وهو القمل أو الجراحة فعليه اذا احتلق فدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expiation options are three days of fasting, feeding six poor people half a sāʿ each of wheat, or sacrificing a sheep.
rows.anchor:
﴿ من صيام ﴾
ثلاثة أيام
﴿ أو صدقة ﴾
على ستة مساكين لكل مسكين نصف صاع من بر
﴿ أو نسك ﴾
وهو شاة

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Ka'b ibn Ujra reports that the Prophet asked whether vermin troubled him; after he said yes, the Prophet told him to shave and choose three days fasting, feeding six needy people or sacrificing a sheep. Ka'b said the verse concerned him.
rows.anchor:
وعن كعب بن عجرة
107 ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له ( لعلك أذاك هوامك ) قال نعم يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet found Ka'b's sore head sufficient harm and ordered him to shave and feed or fast.
rows.anchor: 108 أنه مر به وقد قرح رأسه فقال ( كفى بهذا أذى ) وأمره ان يحلق ويطعم أو يصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nusuk is a verbal noun, or a collective of nasīka; al-Hasan reads nusuk with a light pronunciation.
rows.anchor: والنسك مصدر وقيل جمع نسيكة وقرا الحسن أو ( نسك ) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe means when no longer obstructed and at ease.
rows.anchor: الإحصار يعني فاذا لم تحصروا وكنتم في امن وسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattu means enjoyment or benefit.
rows.anchor: أي استمتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoying Umrah until Hajj means drawing near to God through Umrah before doing so through Hajj.
rows.anchor: واستمتاعه بالعمرة إلى وقت الحج انتفاعه بالتقرب بها إلى الله تعالى قبل الانتفاع بتقربه بالحج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, after completing Umrah one enjoys lawful things formerly forbidden until entering ihram for Hajj.
rows.anchor: وقيل اذا حل من عمرته انتفع باستباحة ما كان محرما عليه إلى ان يحرم بالحج

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa treats the tamattu offering as a ritual and permits the pilgrim to eat from it.
rows.anchor: هو هدي المتعة وهو نسك عند أبي حنيفة وياكل منه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i treats it like an expiation for violations and forbids eating from it.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي يجري مجرى الجنايات ولا يأكل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's school slaughters the tamattu offering on the Day of Sacrifice; al-Shafi'i permits slaughter once the pilgrim enters ihram for Hajj.
rows.anchor: ويذبحه يوم النحر عندنا وعنده يجوز ذبحه اذا أحرم بحجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who lacks the offering must fast three days during the Hajj period, which the Hanafi view places between the Umrah and Hajj ihrams; the preferred days are Tarwiyah, Arafah and the preceding day, and missing the period requires an animal offering.
rows.anchor: أي في وقته وهو أشهره ما بين الإحرامين إحرام العمرة وإحرام الحج وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i permits these fasts only after entering Hajj ihram, following the apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي لا تصام الا بعد الإحرام بالحج تمسكا بظاهر قوله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa understands returning as leaving and finishing the rites of Hajj.
rows.anchor: بمعنى اذا نفرتم وفرغتم من افعال الحج عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i understands returning as going back to one's family.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي هو الرجوع إلى أهاليهم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads 'seven' in the accusative, coordinated with the syntactic position of 'three days.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( وسبعة ) بالنصب عطفا على محل ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The totalizing phrase removes the possible impression that the conjunction offers a choice, as in an instruction to sit with Hasan and Ibn Sirin, which one could fulfill by sitting with either or both.
rows.anchor: الواو قد تجىء للإباحة في نحو قولك جالس الحسن وابن سيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restating the total after its parts makes the number clear from two directions and strengthens certainty, as the proverb says two kinds of knowledge are better than one.
rows.anchor: ففائدة الفذلكة في كل حساب أن يعلم العدد جملة كما علم تفصيلا ليحاط به من جهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāmila adds emphasis, urging completion of every fast without negligence or reduction, like repeating an urgent command not to fall short.
rows.anchor: تاكيد آخر وفيه زيادة توصية بصيامها وأن لا يتهاون بها ولا ينقص من عددها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls the ten complete because they substitute for the offering.
rows.anchor: وقيل كاملة في وقوعها بدلا من الهدي

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading adds that the three fasting days are consecutive.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي ( فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات )
